dedupe_keys.name: space weather mitigation decisions by critical infrastructure operators during solar cycle 25

description: This study examines which space weather mitigation actions power grid, satellite and aviation operators actually took during the peak of Solar Cycle 25, including the May 2024 Gannon storm, the largest space weather event in 20 years. It reviews available mitigation strategies, then reports a survey of 313 operators (50 power, 227 satellite, 36 aviation) with 55 unique responses and qualitative interviews with 33 operators, identifying 91 potential mitigation decisions of which 74 per cent were undertaken; operators favoured low-cost strategies over hardware upgrades, and mission continuity and revenue concerns often led satellite and power operators to bypass conservative protocols. It was written by C. LaNeve, E. J. Oughton, N. T. Rivera, R. S. Weigel, D. Thomas and C. T. Gaunt, posted as a preprint in April 2026 and published in Space Weather on 26 September 2026. The article is available free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the evidence is self-reported by an anonymous, self-selected set of operators, so it is not a complete census of actions. It informs operational response planning for space weather across the energy, space and aviation sectors; a related record is the US National Space Weather Strategy and Action Plan.
